meaning: Fast, unclear talk or baby sounds that make little sense
trick: JAB-JAB-JAB: the mouth jabs out sounds non-stop.
examples: She could hear the baby's hungry grunts, its gurgles and jabbering.
The kids kept jabbering in the back seat all the way home.

usage.pattern: the jabbering of someone / stop jabbering

meaning: Shook hard and fast, like a road drill (informal; here, shivering from cold and fear)
trick: A JACKHAMMER drill shakes the whole body: the cold men jackhammered.
examples: Guys wheezed, coughed, and jackhammered, their eyes wide with terror.
After the ice-cold swim, my whole body jackhammered.

meaning: Shaking hard and fast, like a road drill (informal; here, shivering from cold and fear)
trick: A JACKHAMMER drill never stops shaking: neither do freezing men.
examples: Guys were jackhammering and sniffling, their minds slowly starting to crack.
My heart was jackhammering before the interview.

meaning: A large bath or small pool with jets of warm bubbling water (from a brand name)
trick: JACUZZI: say it fast and it sounds like bubbles going 'zzi-zzi'.
examples: In my dream, I was sitting in a Jacuzzi with him.
The hotel has a pool and a jacuzzi on the roof.

meaning: A hard green stone used for jewellery and carvings; also its light green colour
trick: JADE is a gem that is GREEN: think 'jade green'.
examples: He made these beautiful, jade green swans.
She wore a necklace made of jade.

meaning: Having rough, sharp, uneven edges or points
trick: JAGGED edges JAB you like a saw's teeth.
examples: The jagged pieces of the broken glass fell to the ground.
Be careful, the edge of this tin is jagged.

meaning: A person whose job is to clean and look after a building
trick: JANITOR guards the 'janu-door' (door) and keeps the building clean.
examples: Tariq was hired as a janitor and handyman.
The school janitor mops the floors every evening.

usage.pattern: work as a janitor / the janitor of a building

meaning: Unhappy because someone has something you want; also afraid of losing someone's love to another person
trick: JEALOUS people are 'jal-ous': they jal (burn) inside.
examples: People who pointed out his lazy lifestyle were just "jealous", he said.
My little brother gets jealous when I get new clothes.

meaning: Loud rude shouts or laughs that make fun of someone
trick: JEERS sound like 'cheers' turned nasty: the crowd jeers instead of cheers.
examples: There were heckles and jeers.
The player ignored the jeers from the crowd.

usage.pattern: jeers from someone / be met with jeers

meaning: Moved very fast in one direction, like a jet
hindi: तेज़ी से निकले, फुर्ती से गए
trick: JETTED = moved like a JET.
examples: Several guys dropped their tanks, then jetted to the surface of the pool.
The swimmer jetted across the pool to win the race.

meaning: Rings, necklaces, bracelets, etc. worn for decoration (US spelling; British 'jewellery')
trick: JEWELRY is made of JEWELs.
examples: "Nomad jewelry," she said.
My grandmother gave me her old gold jewelry.

usage.pattern: wear jewelry / a piece of jewelry

meaning: A very short time (informal)
trick: JIFFY = 'Jiff-ee': done in a jiff, in a snap.
examples: He shouted that he'd be with us in a jiffy.
Wait here, I'll be back in a jiffy.

meaning: Made a light ringing sound, like small metal things knocking together
trick: JINGLE BELLS: bells that jingled.
examples: The keys jingled.
The coins jingled in his pocket as he walked.

meaning: Nervous and unable to relax
trick: JITTERY = JITTERs: shaky like too much coffee.
examples: Her own mind was a jittery, muddled mess.
I always feel jittery before an exam.

meaning: To push or shake someone gently; also to run slowly for exercise
trick: JOG someone's shoulder to wake them, JOG in the park to keep fit.
examples: Marie had to jog my shoulders and shout my name to wake me.
I jog in the park every morning.

usage.pattern: jog someone's arm/shoulder / jog someone's memory

meaning: Moved suddenly and roughly; also shocked or surprised
trick: JOLTED: like a jolt of electricity making you jump.
examples: The woman's head jolted back as if he had thrown a brick at her.
The bus jolted to a stop and everyone fell forward.

meaning: Sudden rough shakes or movements; also sudden shocks
trick: JOLTS on a bumpy road JOLT your bones.
examples: The glare, the smell of gasoline and the jolts made me feel drowsy.
The old bus gave us painful jolts on the rough road.

usage.pattern: the jolts of something / with jolts

meaning: Pushing roughly against others in a crowd, often to get somewhere first
trick: JOSTLING = JUST pushing to get in front.
examples: The children were jostling with one another to climb into her arms.
People were jostling to get on the crowded train.

usage.pattern: jostle with someone / jostle for something / to do something

meaning: Cheerful and friendly in a warm, hearty way
trick: JOVIAL = JOLLY + JOY: always smiling.
examples: Mariam remembered the jovial way he had pushed his gifts at her.
Our jovial neighbour always greets us with a joke.

meaning: Full of joy; very happy
trick: JOYOUS = full of JOY.
examples: They are some of the most meaningful and joyous things we'll ever do.
The wedding was a joyous day for the whole family.

meaning: Extremely happy and excited, especially because of a success
trick: JUBILANT people celebrate a JUBILEE.
examples: She pictured Zalmai's jubilant, running welcomes when Rasheed came home.
The jubilant fans danced after their team won.

usage.pattern: be jubilant (at/about something) / a jubilant + noun

meaning: To deal with several tasks or problems at the same time; also to keep several objects in the air by throwing and catching
hindi: कई काम एक साथ संभालना; करतब से गेंदें उछालना
trick: A JUGGLER keeps many balls up, like you juggle work and home.
examples: This drill tested our ability to juggle several stresses at once.
Many mothers juggle a job and a family.

usage.pattern: juggle something (and something) / juggle multiple things

meaning: Someone who is very keen on something (informal); also a drug addict
trick: JUNKIE: hooked on something, like junk food.
examples: Erin is a self-improvement junkie.
My brother is a news junkie who reads every paper.

meaning: An area, or the official power, where a court or authority can make legal decisions
trick: JURIS = law (like jury, justice) + DICTION = speaking: where the law speaks.
examples: New York has more hostage negotiation jobs than any other jurisdiction in the country.
This case is outside the local court's jurisdiction.

usage.pattern: within/outside someone's jurisdiction / have jurisdiction over something

meaning: A group of ordinary people who listen to a court case and decide if someone is guilty
trick: JURY decides like a JUDGE, but they are ordinary people.
examples: These people were staring hard at me, and I guessed they were the jury.
The jury found him not guilty.

usage.pattern: the jury finds someone guilty/not guilty / serve on a jury

meaning: Men who are members of a jury (old-fashioned)
trick: JURY + MEN = the men on the jury.
examples: The jurymen were all gazing at the red-robed judge.
The twelve jurymen listened carefully to the witness.

meaning: Sticking out beyond the edge or surface of something
trick: JUT = just out: a rock JUTTING out of the cliff.
examples: There's a small rock jutting out of the cliff side.
He hurt his knee on a nail jutting out of the wall.

meaning: A young person who is not yet an adult, especially in law; also childish
trick: JUVENILE = JUNIOR in law: not yet an adult.
examples: Children from abusive homes are more likely to be arrested as a juvenile.
The boy was sent to a home for juveniles.

usage.pattern: as a juvenile / juvenile + noun (court, crime)
